solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female novelist wanting women's expression of disgust

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following item is taken away from the preceding name

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh, English novelist
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A woman writer is short of women's expressions of revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: F plus WAUGH, with the W removed, gives FAUGH; the 's reads as 'is' to join wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Faugh is an old interjection voicing contempt or revulsion, like 'ugh'.

clue.text: Brother with me in court for conspiracy

parts.note: Fra is the title of an Italian friar, a brother
taken as written
someone up before the magistrates is in court

explanation.surface: A monk and the speaker find themselves in the dock accused of plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame-up is a plot to make an innocent person appear guilty, a kind of conspiracy.

clue.text: I'll transfer right like an Italian gent

parts.note: as means like
Signor is the Italian for Mr, a gentleman

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman promises to hand over his rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the answer's own voice: the person speaking is one who assigns a right.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an assignor is the party who transfers a right or property to another.

clue.text: Where one learns trade — it's far from perfect

parts.note: short for university, a place of learning
to deal is to trade

explanation.surface: Learning a trade at college is a poor arrangement, someone complains.
explanation.definitionFit: Unideal simply means not ideal, so falling well short of perfection.

clue.text: Woopies swapping money for daughter's flowers

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means one letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: glams (greying, leisured, affluent, married) are well-off older people, like woopies
M is the abbreviation for money
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Well-off retirees spend less on themselves and buy their daughter flowers instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Woopies (well-off older persons) and glams are both acronyms Chambers lists for comfortable older people; replace the M of GLAMS with D.
explanation.definitionFit: Glads is the informal shortening of gladioli, the tall spiky garden flowers.

clue.text: Carved lances left with devastating tapers

indicators.note: something carved has been cut into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

indicators.note: the left end of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the leftmost letter of this word

explanation.surface: Knights' lances are whittled down into deadly thin spikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Devastating tapers' looks like a phrase, but 'devastating' only supplies its left-hand letter to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle, so tapers are candles.

clue.text: Poke fun at English CBer … she's a cracker

parts.note: to cod is to hoax or tease someone
E is the abbreviation for English
a breaker is a user of citizens' band radio, from the call 'breaker' used to join a channel

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an English radio ham, who turns out to be quite something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' looks like praise for a woman, but it means one who cracks codes.
explanation.definitionFit: A codebreaker cracks ciphers, so she is literally a cracker.

clue.text: Take home tails from these birds which Greeks plucked

parts.note: take-home pay is net pay, so to take home is to net

indicators.note: tails are the end parts, so the last letter of each named word is kept

parts.note: the final letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Collect the tail feathers of birds the Greeks once plucked for the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucked' suggests poultry being prepared, but it means strings plucked on a lyre: a nete was the highest string of the Greek lyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Netes were strings of the ancient Greek lyre, played by plucking.

clue.text: Merchants run for one in nappies

indicators.note: one thing given for another means it takes that thing's place in a word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral one
diapers is the American word for nappies

explanation.surface: Traders are selling their nappies on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I of DIAPERS for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapers are merchants who deal in cloth and textiles.

clue.text: Pick up small scratch from old Greek wolves

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up raises letters so they read from the bottom upward

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
scratch is slang for money, and an obol was an ancient Greek coin

explanation.surface: Collect a little cash from an elderly Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: S and OBOL together, read upwards, give LOBOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobo is the Spanish-derived name for the timber wolf of the American south-west.

clue.text: Difficult to douse completely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... climb or task is hard
second meaning: to soak something thoroughly in liquid

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one awkward chore; it is two unrelated meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is an adjective for something hard going and a verb for soaking thoroughly, as with tea.

clue.text: Moved up support for flower in rockery?

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise
to root for a team is to support it

explanation.surface: A gardener lifted a prop for a plant in the rock garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: this plant suits rock gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseroot is a fleshy sedum with rose-scented roots, often grown among rocks.

clue.text: Hot caterer's whipped cream may be served with this

definitions.text: cream may be served with this

indicators.note: whipped means beaten about, so these letters are thrashed into a new order

parts.note: every letter including the S is used

explanation.surface: A busy cook's whipped cream goes on a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whipped cream' reads as one phrase, but 'whipped' acts on the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachertorte, the Viennese chocolate cake, is traditionally served with unsweetened whipped cream.

clue.text: Floridly written in the style of Fleming, amongst others

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Ian Fleming, creator of James Bond, is one of many called Ian

explanation.surface: A spy-novel pastiche is overwritten in the manner of Fleming and others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the style of Fleming' suggests imitation of his prose, but Fleming just stands for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records Asian as describing an ornate, florid literary style, from the ancient Asiatic school of rhetoric.

clue.text: Duke with a bit of furniture having provenance

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
taken as written
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A duke owns an antique table with a documented history.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a known provenance can be assigned an age and origin, so it can be dated.

clue.text: A point of reference such as the fifth letter from church officer?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a fixed point used for orientation; the musical note at the centre of the keyboard is a tuning reference

definitions.text: such as the fifth letter from church officer?
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a church officer who teaches the catechism has nine letters, and the fifth is a C that sits exactly in the centre

explanation.walkthrough: The church officer is a CATECHIST; its fifth letter is the C right in the middle, hence a middle C.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the note near the centre of the piano keyboard, the standard reference pitch for reading music.

clue.text: Term for verse mostly behind lyric

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a name for a type of poetry
setter's reading: the closing section of a Greek choral ode, which comes after the strophe and antistrophe of the lyric

explanation.walkthrough: The Greek name means 'after-song': in a choral ode the epode follows the strophe and antistrophe, so it sits behind the bulk of the lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: An epode is the third, concluding stanza of a Greek ode, and also a lyric form with long and short lines alternating.

clue.text: Légionnaire's final exploit no longer causes discharge

indicators.note: final points to the end of the word, so its last letter alone is used

parts.note: the last letter of the soldier, ignoring the possessive
gest is an archaic word for a notable deed or exploit; no longer flags it as obsolete

explanation.surface: A Foreign Legion soldier's last daring deed leads to his dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests a soldier dismissed from service; here it is the bodily sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to expel waste matter from the body, to discharge it.

clue.text: Comment is twisted and mean

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of its normal shape, so these two letters change places

parts.note: the two letters swapped round
to denote is to mean or signify

explanation.surface: A remark that is spiteful and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted and mean' looks like two insults; 'mean' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A side note is a remark written in the margin, a comment beside the main text.

clue.text: Country walk being with dog

parts.note: one's nature is one's essential being
to dog someone is to follow or trail them

explanation.surface: A walk in the countryside accompanied by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A nature trail is a signposted path through the countryside for observing wildlife.

clue.text: Paying tax borders on technicality — fact

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: its edge letters
a thing can mean a fact, as in 'the thing is'

explanation.surface: Paying tax comes down to a technicality, and that is a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: TYTHING is an obsolete spelling of tithing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithing is the paying of a tenth of one's produce or income as a tax to the church.

clue.text: Funky loos are getting a spray

indicators.note: funky suggests something unconventional and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Smelly toilets are getting a blast of air freshener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funky' reads as smelly, which suits the toilets, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that releases its contents as a fine spray.

clue.text: Judge facetiously checking charge lit up in the old way

definitions.text: lit up in the old way

indicators.note: checking means holding back or restraining, so one word is held within another

parts.note: 'm'lud' is a jokey rendering of 'my lord', the form used to address a judge
a mine is an explosive charge

explanation.surface: A judge, joking, keeps an eye on a case lit by old-fashioned lamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee or an accusation in court, but here it is an explosive one; 'in the old way' flags an obsolete verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumine is an obsolete verb meaning to illuminate, so lumined meant lit up.

clue.text: Sperm oil mixed with dye changed into something like PVC

indicators.note: mixed means blended together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Whale oil blended with colouring has been turned into a kind of plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Polymerised describes molecules joined into long chains, which is how plastics such as PVC are made.

clue.text: Mottled Journal, aged, special within

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for journal

indicators.note: within means inside, so this item sits inside the one before it

parts.note: ae, short for Latin aetatis, means aged, as on memorials
SP is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: An old, special diary has a marbled cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads like a catalogue entry for an old diary, but each item after the definition is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaspé describes a mottled, jasper-like finish on cloth or pottery.

clue.text: Instruments going west in main rocket

indicators.note: west is leftward on a map, so the letters are read right to left
in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: letters inside the two words

explanation.surface: Equipment heading west inside the main rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry 'going west' would be standard; in a down clue it still just means read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Corni is the Italian plural of corno, the French horn, an orchestral brass instrument.

clue.text: Seemingly learned clodhopper cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a baboon is a clumsy, boorish person

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf is told to keep it brief.
explanation.walkthrough: BABOO, from colonial India, was a clerk whose English education was thought superficial, so learned only in appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboo was an Indian clerk with a show of English learning, hence seemingly learned.

clue.text: Arab in skirt found here

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, here wrapped by the garment's edge

parts.note: to skirt is to edge, and a hem is the edge of a skirt
AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A place where skirted Arab women might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: this is where the women of a traditional Arab household would be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a traditional Muslim household.

clue.text: Love yawning

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek word for selfless, spiritual love
second meaning: wide open, as a gaping mouth

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: three syllables for love, two for open-mouthed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape is Christian brotherly love; agape also means gaping wide open.

clue.text: Greetings from Honalo, Hawaii

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: letters inside, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Postcard greetings from a town in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: Honalo is a real place on Hawaii's Big Island, which makes the hiding place look innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used as a greeting and farewell.

clue.text: No good in retreat backing one African beast

indicators.note: in puts one item inside another
backing means going backwards, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a nook is a secluded retreat
NG is the abbreviation for no good
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A troop pulls back with one of the herd: no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast is not one of the famous big animals but a less familiar antelope with a Swahili name.
explanation.definitionFit: The kongoni is the Coke's hartebeest, an East African antelope.

clue.text: Scruple about ripe Brie — it's the writer's point

indicators.note: a cheese so ripe it runs about loses its shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: scr. is the abbreviation for scruple, an apothecaries' weight
the cheese rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has qualms about runny cheese, but it is the author's point.
explanation.definitionFit: A scriber is a sharp-pointed tool used to mark lines on wood or metal, a scratching pen.

clue.text: Native of Morocco is a charitable sort

parts.note: MA is the international vehicle code for Morocco
a native is a son of the place where he was born

explanation.surface: A man born in Morocco is a generous person.
explanation.walkthrough: The native is a son of Morocco, so the son follows the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons are known for their charitable work, so a mason can be described as a charitable sort.

clue.text: Can Scots market upset husband's good bargain?

parts.note: the can is slang for prison, as is the pen

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a tron was a public weighing machine and market place in Scottish burghs
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A tin of something from a Scottish market is a husband's great find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' at the start looks like a verb opening a question, but it is a noun; the answer is a contraction of pennyworth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennorth is a pennyworth, a small amount bought, and Chambers gives 'a good pennyworth' as a bargain.

clue.text: Mostly impressive and inspired imitator

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: epic means grand or impressive
gone can mean infatuated, carried away, as one inspired

explanation.surface: A copycat artist who is mostly impressive and full of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigone is an undistinguished follower or imitator of a great artist.

clue.text: Notice containing Latin concealed by some

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one item wraps the other

parts.note: to heed is to notice or take note
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A notice in Latin was hidden by some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By some' signals a dialect word, used only in certain regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hele is a dialect verb meaning to hide or cover, so heled means concealed.
